newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent drifts lower in dull holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent drifts lower in dull holiday trade.

text.p: IPE Brent futures stagnated at lower levels on Thursday as public holidays across most of Europe took their toll of trade, trader said.
June IPE Brent was trading 10 cents lower at $18.41 a barrel 1206 GMT, while May gas oil was 25 cents off at $171.50 a tonne.
Traders attributed a downward blip to $18.36 seen around 1150 GMT to the sale of positions taken by various players in earlier trade after a U.S. broker came in for 500-700 lots.
"I think the market was a bit mystified about the broker's intentions so a number of players followed suit and bought as well," one trader.
"But now it appears there was nothing behind it and the market has come off accordingly."
Beyond the downward blip, the market was fairly featureless, with the absence of many continental European players muting trade.
"The European holidays have killed the market for today and probably tomorrow," said another trader. "We might see New York taking the opportunity to manipulate prices."
Traders said the gap to $18.77 remained an important target for the June Brent contract. It climbed as high as $18.75 on Wednesday before turning tail.
"I don't think we'll see too much price action. People won't want to be higher territory in such thin volumes," the trader said.
